result: The authors developed a chimeric DNA sequence (CCEN) combining native centromeric sequences (CDEII and CDEIII) with Widom 601 DNA that stably wraps centromeric histone octamers and can be purified by size-exclusion chromatography. This chimera includes 35 bp of CDEII (containing the Mif2 footprint), all of CDEIII, and flanking Widom 601 sequences.
evaluation: All reviewers acknowledge the successful development of the CCEN chimera. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'use a hybrid DNA sequence that combines CDEII and CDEIII as well as Widom 601 so they can make stable histones for biophysical studies.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'the authors now report that they were able to replace part of the Widom 601 DNA with centromeric DNA from chromosome 3.' The editor notes this 'builds upon previous studies' successfully.

result: OA-based kinetochore assemblies withstood significantly higher rupture forces when assembled on CCEN-NCPs (median 6.0 pN) compared to W601-NCPs (median 4.2 pN, p=1.87×10⁻⁶), demonstrating that centromeric DNA sequences strengthen OA-mediated linkages and revealing new DNA sequence preferences for OA.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly support this finding. The editor states the work 'convincingly show[s] that the centromere-histone core contributes to force transduction through the kinetochore.' Reviewer 1 notes 'the Centromere core of Widom and CDE II and III contribute to strengthening the binding force for the OA-beads. The data are very nicely done and convincingly demonstrate the point.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'the presence of the centromeric DNA fragment makes one type of minimal kinetochore assembly...withstand stronger forces.'

result: Mif2-based kinetochore assemblies showed no significant strengthening with CCEN-NCPs (median 2.9 pN) compared to W601-NCPs (median 2.5 pN, p=0.302), despite CCEN containing the complete Mif2 footprint from CDEII.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding but note it was unexpected. Reviewer 2 states 'Which kinetochore assembly turned out to be affected was somewhat unexpected, and can currently not be reconciled with structural knowledge of the budding yeast centromere/kinetochore.' The editor acknowledges 'the centromere mainly strengthens one of the two paths of force transduction.' The data itself is not questioned, only its interpretation relative to existing knowledge.

result: Functional kinetochore assemblies formed on both CCEN-NCPs and W601-NCPs with either OA or Mif2 present (>78% microtubule binding), while negative controls without OA or Mif2 showed 0% binding, confirming that both inner kinetochore proteins can independently support kinetochore assembly on the chimeric centromeric nucleosomes.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these control experiments without criticism. Reviewer 2 notes this work 'confirmed previous findings that OA and Mif2 can independently support recombinant kinetochore assembly' using the new CCEN DNA. The functional assembly data validates the experimental system and is treated as confirmatory rather than novel.

result: The findings indicate that centromeric DNA sequences are important for force transmission through the kinetochore, making significant contributions to attachment strength between the inner kinetochore and centromeric nucleosome, with differential effects depending on whether DNA is wrapped around nucleosomes versus presented as free DNA.
evaluation: The editor explicitly states the work 'convincingly show[s] that the centromere-histone core contributes to force transduction through the kinetochore' and that 'the centromere mainly strengthens one of the two paths of force transduction, influenced by the centromeric DNA sequence.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'the paper demonstrates that centromeric DNA can increase the attachment strength between budding yeast microtubules and centromeric nucleosomes.'

result: The authors propose potential mechanisms for the observed effects, including that CCEN DNA might present the Cse4 N-terminus more favorably to OA, that OA might show sequence preferences only with wrapped DNA, and that Mif2 might require more than its footprinted binding site for full DNA sequence specificity.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge these are speculative interpretations. Reviewer 1 notes 'the weakness is that this is the entire paper' and that 'beyond that the impact is fairly limited in scope.' Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'How centromeric DNA exerts this effect remains unclear' and notes 'In the future, it will be interesting to pinpoint which interactions contribute to the enhanced force resistance.' The mechanisms are presented as possibilities requiring future investigation.

result: CCEN represents an advance toward working with a more native-like recombinant kinetochore system for studying force transmission.
evaluation: Reviewers treat this as a valuable methodological advance. Reviewer 2 states 'This makes the assay more closely resemble the in vivo situation' and calls it 'a valuable addendum to the findings described in Hamilton et al. 2020.' The editor describes it as 'valuable research advance' that 'builds upon previous studies.' However, Reviewer 1 notes the 'impact is fairly limited in scope' beyond kinetochore specialists.
